# Amazon Redshift Serverless

Manage namespaces, workgroups, snapshots, usage limits and private endpoint records without a warehouse.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `redshiftserverless` |
| Signing name | `redshift-serverless` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.1 |
| API version | `2021-04-21` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Configuration records only |
| Selected operations | 30 of 65 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#amazon-redshift-serverless) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- No SQL engine, recovery points, scheduled actions, custom domains, reservations, managed workgroups, tracks, resource policies, cross-account access or snapshot copy.
- CloudFormation DbName updates fail explicitly because UpdateNamespace has no dbName member; unsupported properties and property removal fail explicitly.
- Usage limits and endpoint access are metadata only; no usage enforcement or network interface allocation.
- Temporary credentials expire after 900-3600 seconds but authenticate no engine; snapshot retention is metadata, without automatic expiry.
- Regional RPU availability and capacity quotas are not enforced; metadata accepts documented base-capacity increments up to 1024 RPUs and Max capacity -1 or 4-5632 RPUs.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
